title: On Realising the danger far too late
subtitle: 成功成就 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 成功成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）
meta: 主题语境：成功成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）　|　核心词汇：realise　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 realise 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1979 the counsellor ① realised the danger far too late without complaint, and every listener in the garden said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three evenings on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the counsellor ② realises the danger far too late with great care without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ realise the danger far too late at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ realised the danger far too late before — a line in the journal for June 1973 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Realising the danger far too late without complaint, the counsellor said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the letter at the far bench, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ realise the wish of twenty years with great care, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Realise the wish of twenty years at once and never mention it again.

By 1986 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the journal, and a new listener from the next garden ⑧ realises the wish of twenty years without complaint every evening without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the bench, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ realised the danger far too late again when nobody else would.

⑩ To realise the danger far too late, my mother said in 1991, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the garden remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the garden forgets, somebody realises the danger far too late with great care again and somebody must realise the danger far too late without complaint all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 意识到（一般过去式 realised the danger far too late：1979 年谈心人头一回这样做，毫无怨言地）
B. v. 意识到（一般现在 realises the danger far too late：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 意识到（不定式 to realise the danger far too late：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 意识到（过去完成时 had realised the danger far too late：1973 年六月的心记上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 意识到（动名词 realising the danger far too late 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 实现（realise the wish of twenty years：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去实现实现了二十年前的那个愿望）
G. v. 实现（realise the wish of twenty years：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 意识到（后段两处：新来的倾听者照例 realises the wish of twenty years，而母亲又一次 realised the danger far too late）

answers.why: realise 意为“意识到”，1979 年谈心人毫无怨言地意识到意识到那份危险时已太迟，那是小园里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 realised。
realise 意为“意识到”，自那以后谈心人小心翼翼地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 realises。
realise 意为“意识到”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯意识到意识到那份危险时已太迟”，此处为不定式 to realise the danger far too late。
realise 意为“意识到”，心记里 六月 那行字说明早在 1986 年之前就有人意识到过，故用过去完成时 had realised。
realise 意为“意识到”，谈心人说“意识到意识到那份危险时已太迟这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 realising the danger far too late 作主语。
realise 意为“实现”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去实现实现了二十年前的那个愿望”，should ever 之后用原形 realise the wish of twenty years。
realise 意为“实现”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻实现实现了二十年前的那个愿望（realise the wish of twenty years at once），以后再也不要提起。
realise 意为“意识到”，新来的倾听者每个黄昏都照例实现实现了二十年前的那个愿望，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 realises。
realise 意为“意识到”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次毫无怨言地意识到意识到那份危险时已太迟，用一般过去式 realised 叙述。
realise 意为“意识到”，结尾那句是母亲 1991 年的话：要意识到意识到那份危险时已太迟，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和小园记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 realise 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1979 the counsellor realised the danger far too late without complaint, and nobody in the garden forgot it.
Even now the counsellor realises the danger far too late with great care whenever the garden asks.
Realising the danger far too late without complaint, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever realise the wish of twenty years with great care, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new listener from the next garden realises the wish of twenty years without complaint every evening, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother realised the danger far too late again, and the garden remembered that half.
